import pandas as pd

# File paths for source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/test_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/test_2.csv"
source3_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/test_3.csv"
source4_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/test_4.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # ['Institution', 'year 2016']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # ['Institution', 'year 2014']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # ['Institution', '(Fall 2000)', ..., '(Fall 2014)']
df3 = pd.read_csv(source3_path, index_col=0)  # ['Institution', 'year 2015']
df4 = pd.read_csv(source4_path, index_col=0)  # ['Institution', 'Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016']

# Rename columns in df0, df1, df3 to match target columns
# year 2014 -> persist 2014 (int)
# year 2015 -> persist 2015 (int)
# year 2016 -> persist 2016 (int)
df0_renamed = df0.rename(columns={"year 2016": "persist 2016"})
df1_renamed = df1.rename(columns={"year 2014": "persist 2014"})
df3_renamed = df3.rename(columns={"year 2015": "persist 2015"})

# Convert persist columns to integer (they should already be int, but ensure)
df0_renamed["persist 2016"] = df0_renamed["persist 2016"].astype(int)
df1_renamed["persist 2014"] = df1_renamed["persist 2014"].astype(int)
df3_renamed["persist 2015"] = df3_renamed["persist 2015"].astype(int)

# Select only relevant columns (Institution + persist columns)
df0_sel = df0_renamed[["Institution", "persist 2016"]]
df1_sel = df1_renamed[["Institution", "persist 2014"]]
df3_sel = df3_renamed[["Institution", "persist 2015"]]

# From df2, select Institution and the Fall columns needed in target:
# '(Fall 2011)', '(Fall 2012)', '(Fall 2013)', '(Fall 2014)'
fall_cols = ['Institution', '(Fall 2011)', '(Fall 2012)', '(Fall 2013)', '(Fall 2014)']
df2_sel = df2[fall_cols].copy()

# From df4, select Institution and Cohort columns
cohort_cols = ['Institution', 'Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016']
df4_sel = df4[cohort_cols].copy()

# Ensure Cohort columns are integer type (in source they are float)
df4_sel['Cohort 2014'] = df4_sel['Cohort 2014'].fillna(0).astype(int)
df4_sel['Cohort 2015'] = df4_sel['Cohort 2015'].fillna(0).astype(int)
df4_sel['Cohort 2016'] = df4_sel['Cohort 2016'].fillna(0).astype(int)

# Merge all dataframes on 'Institution' using outer join to keep all institutions
# Start merging df2_sel (Fall data) with persist dataframes and cohort dataframe

# Merge Fall data with persist 2014 (df1_sel)
merged = pd.merge(df2_sel, df1_sel, on='Institution', how='outer')

# Merge with persist 2015 (df3_sel)
merged = pd.merge(merged, df3_sel, on='Institution', how='outer')

# Merge with persist 2016 (df0_sel)
merged = pd.merge(merged, df0_sel, on='Institution', how='outer')

# Merge with cohort data (df4_sel)
merged = pd.merge(merged, df4_sel, on='Institution', how='outer')

# After merges, some columns may have NaNs due to missing data in some sources.
# For float columns (Fall years), keep NaN as is (or optionally fill with NaN).
# For integer columns (persist and cohort), fill NaN with 0 and convert to int.

persist_cols = ['persist 2014', 'persist 2015', 'persist 2016']
cohort_cols = ['Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016']

for col in persist_cols + cohort_cols:
    merged[col] = merged[col].fillna(0).astype(int)

# Ensure Fall columns are float type (they should be already)
fall_year_cols = ['(Fall 2011)', '(Fall 2012)', '(Fall 2013)', '(Fall 2014)']
for col in fall_year_cols:
    merged[col] = pd.to_numeric(merged[col], errors='coerce')

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = ['Institution', '(Fall 2011)', '(Fall 2012)', '(Fall 2013)', '(Fall 2014)',
                  'persist 2014', 'persist 2015', 'persist 2016',
                  'Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016']

merged = merged[target_columns]

# Sort by Institution alphabetically for neatness (optional)
merged = merged.sort_values(by='Institution').reset_index(drop=True)

# Write the result to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/target_multisource_cot.csv"
merged.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/test_0.csv", index_col=0)  # ['Institution', 'year 2016']
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/test_1.csv", index_col=0)  # ['Institution', 'year 2014']
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/test_2.csv", index_col=0)  # ['Institution', '(Fall 2000)', ..., '(Fall 2014)']
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/test_3.csv", index_col=0)  # ['Institution', 'year 2015']
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/test_4.csv", index_col=0)  # ['Institution', 'Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016']

# Step 1: Rename year columns to persist columns for clarity before join
source0_renamed = source0.rename(columns={"year 2016": "persist 2016"})
source1_renamed = source1.rename(columns={"year 2014": "persist 2014"})
source3_renamed = source3.rename(columns={"year 2015": "persist 2015"})

# Step 2: Join source1 and source3 on Institution (persist 2014 and persist 2015)
persist_14_15 = pd.merge(source1_renamed, source3_renamed, on="Institution", how="inner")

# Step 3: Join the above with source0 (persist 2016)
persist_all = pd.merge(persist_14_15, source0_renamed, on="Institution", how="inner")

# Step 4: From source2, select columns for (Fall 2011) to (Fall 2014) plus Institution
fall_cols = ['Institution', '(Fall 2011)', '(Fall 2012)', '(Fall 2013)', '(Fall 2014)']
fall_data = source2[fall_cols]

# Step 5: From source4, select Institution and Cohort columns (Cohort 2014, Cohort 2015, Cohort 2016)
cohort_cols = ['Institution', 'Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016']
cohort_data = source4[cohort_cols]

# Step 6: Join fall_data with persist_all on Institution
df = pd.merge(fall_data, persist_all, on="Institution", how="inner")

# Step 7: Join the above with cohort_data on Institution
df = pd.merge(df, cohort_data, on="Institution", how="inner")

# Step 8: According to FD, Institution is the key, so group by Institution to ensure uniqueness
# Aggregate float columns by mean and integer columns by sum to handle any duplicates

    {**{col: 'mean' for col in float_cols},

)

for col in int_cols:

# Step 10: Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = ['Institution', '(Fall 2011)', '(Fall 2012)', '(Fall 2013)', '(Fall 2014)',
                  'persist 2014', 'persist 2015', 'persist 2016',
                  'Cohort 2014', 'Cohort 2015', 'Cohort 2016']

result = df_grouped[target_columns]

# Step 11: Sort by Institution alphabetically for neatness (optional)
result = result.sort_values('Institution').reset_index(drop=True)

# Write the result to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_82/target_multisource_critique_history.csv"
